sessionTitle: Build realtime multimodal agents with LiveKit and Azure

announcements.name: End-to-end voice agent built on Azure plus LiveKit
announcements.shortDescription: Azure can serve all three pipeline stages: Azure STT, OpenAI through Azure for the LLM, and Azure TTS.
announcements.longDescription: LiveKit is model agnostic and lets developers pick which STT, LLM, and TTS models to use in the voice pipeline, mixing and matching with one line of code to swap a model. Azure fits into all three stages: Azure STT for speech-to-text, OpenAI through Azure for the LLM, and Azure TTS for text-to-speech. The agent's SDK at the orchestration layer is where custom code, tools, MCP servers, and business logic connect media to the model.

announcements.name: Live demo of a completed Build assistant
announcements.shortDescription: A customized agent greets the user and correctly answers that Microsoft Build 2026 runs June 2–3 in San Francisco at Fort Mason, with an online experience.
announcements.longDescription: A customized agent with a Microsoft Build themed front end greets the user warmly and offers help with Microsoft technologies like Azure, Windows, Microsoft 365, and GitHub. When asked for the dates, the computer voice correctly answers that Microsoft Build 2026 takes place June 2nd and June 3rd, a two-day event in San Francisco at Fort Mason with an online experience. The demo uses Azure STT and Azure TTS with a defined voice, plus a Solero [inferred] (Silero) VAD model, started in dev mode.

announcements.name: LiveKit MCP docs server and skill
announcements.shortDescription: Recommended as the most important tooling so coding agents build against up-to-date LiveKit context, given near-weekly feature shipping.
announcements.longDescription: The speaker recommends using the LiveKit MCP docs server or the skill as the most important tooling to ensure coding agents build against up-to-date LiveKit context. Because LiveKit ships new features almost every week and the docs are always kept current, a coding agent needs the most complete context to build accurately. The speaker prefers the MCP server for this purpose.
